plans_dgz.md - HowMaHiCo

Source: plans_dgz.md

What this is

Plans by DGZ to improve HowMaHiCo.

Instructions: when prompted, you can read this file and provide a plan to do the pending tasks in “to do”. When something is done, move it to the end of “Done”. Do not consider the points in “In standby”, until they are moved to “to do”

To do

Road to the EuPA 2026 abstract (example/abstract_eupa2026_v3.md)

Gap analysis of the package (v0.18.0) against the submitted abstract text, in priority order. Tier A must be true before the abstract is submitted, tier B before the meeting, tier C is wording-vs-code mismatches that can be closed either by implementing or by re-wording the abstract.

Tier A — blocking, the abstract makes these promises explicitly

  • make the GitHub repo public. The abstract prints https://github.com/DavidGZ1/HowMaHiCo, which currently 404s (gh repo view: isPrivate: true), and GitHub Pages will not serve gh-pages from a private repo, so https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/ is dead too. While there: fill in the empty repo description + homepage field, add a CITATION.cff, and mint a Zenodo DOI so the poster has something citable.
  • DONE (v0.23.0) — license conflict resolved: relicensed to GPL (>= 2) (not plain GPL-3: Peptides, gplots and ggcorrplot are GPL-2 only).
  • abstract housekeeping: the affiliation is still the placeholder [Affiliation: institution, city, country]; decide whether the submission carries the institutional address or DESCRIPTION’s davidgz.science@gmail.com.

Tier B — needed before the meeting; the abstract’s Results/Conclusions rest on them

  • demonstration dataset + actual results. The Results paragraph is capability prose with no numbers, no figure and no comparison, and the only shipped data is inst/extdata/sim_fragpipe_dda (462 synthetic peptides, FragPipe DDA only) — fine for tests, not for a poster panel. Need at least one real dataset rendered end to end, class 1 and class 2 (the advanced-plans “JY hla1 and hla2 from Annica and Julian” item), ideally with a PRIDE accession so the QC claims are reproducible. Highest-value single panel: the quality score separating a genuine immunopeptidome from a failed pulldown / whole-proteome negative control — that is the figure that demonstrates “how MHC is the dataset”.
  • DONE (v0.25.0, 09_overview) — general-overview report for the biologically focused user (the advanced-plans “Simple summary of HowMaHiCo ala HowDirty” item). The abstract promises “a general-overview report for biologically focused users and another for deeper evaluation by the LC-MS expert”; what exists is 8 thematic slices plus 00_mhc_report, a ~1300-line all-in-one that is the opposite of an overview (and the legacy report where the Overlap intra-Condition bug is still uncorrected). 03_lcms_qc already covers the expert half. Scope: one page — counts, length-window fidelity, quality score, red flags.
  • DONE (v0.24.0) — cross-experiment comparison, claimed in the Conclusions but not implemented: one render = one subset, and nothing stacks the per-sample score CSVs that 05_quality_score writes into a trend view. Add a compare_runs() reading N score tables (+ a longitudinal/trend plot per metric) so the sentence becomes true.

Tier C — code does not match the wording; implement or re-word

  • DONE (v0.21.0) - “interactive HTML” is overstated. Interactivity today = tabsets + floating TOC, DT tables in 06/07/08, and exactly two ggplotly() calls (00_mhc_report L996/L1034, 04_quant L118/L156); every other plot is a static raster. Either land the standby InteractivePlots toggle for the plots that are not inside results='asis' loops (correlation, PCA, volcano, dynamic range, completeness are the easy ones) or soften the abstract to “self-contained, navigable HTML”.
  • DONE (v0.20.0) — class 2 in the title vs. the quality score: for MHCclass = "MHC2", qc_metrics_by_sample() returns NA for frac_9mer and anchor_information (no fixed-length anchor model), so they drop out of the composite — the “motif clarity” the Results paragraph names is not delivered for class 2, although the title claims “class 1 and class 2”. Either add a register-free class-2 motif metric (positional entropy over a sliding 9-mer core) or qualify the sentence.
  • DONE (v0.20.0) — mass error is absent for DIA-NN (ppm is a hardcoded 0 dummy, documented and dropped from the score), so “identification QC such as score and mass error” is hollow for the DIA audience. Derivable from Precursor.Mz vs the theoretical m/z of sequence + PTM if it is worth making real.
  • DONE (v0.19.0) — PTM profiles are unreadable as shipped: UniMod codes for DIA-NN, bare delta masses for FragPipe/PEAKS. R/ptm.R (ptm_reference() + translate_ptm()) now translates both forms, wired into plot_ptm_heatmap(translate = TRUE).
  • DONE (v0.22.0) — verify PEAKS Xpro before it appears in print. It did not work: read_peaks_batch() filtered export folders by the per-sample key (Sample_peaks) instead of Sample_folder, and pasted an absolute FolderData behind getwd(). Both fixed, both now failing loudly, and inst/extdata/sim_peaks_xpro/ + tests cover the path end to end. Still open for DGZ: run it against a REAL PEAKS 11/Xpro export — a simulated one cannot prove column-name parity.
  • “for both non-coders and advanced programmers” is present tense in the Background, but the workflow needs R, a hand-edited annotation CSV and a render call; get_pipeline_script() + demo mode soften it, and Docker/Shiny are correctly labelled “planned”. Low risk — re-read it once the Shiny tier exists.
  • DONE (v0.19.0) — finish the glossaries, which the abstract’s reproducibility framing leans on: pep_all_glossary() + inst/rmarkdown/shared/glossary.Rmd now generate both the in-report glossary (in all ten templates) and the README table from one function. Still open for DGZ: read the 30 descriptions and correct anything that is wrong.

to be done by DGZ

  • Check and complete glosary - NOW GENERATED: the 30 column descriptions live in pep_all_glossary() (R/report-helpers.R) and feed both the in-report glossary (inst/rmarkdown/shared/glossary.Rmd, in all ten templates) and the README table. They were written by Claude from the loaders + CLAUDE.md, so read them once and correct anything wrong; the tests only check that every required column IS documented, never that the text is right (v0.19.0)
  • check/add functionality for peaks Xpro - the two blocking bugs are fixed and covered by a simulated export (v0.22.0), but run it on a real PEAKS 11/Xpro export: a simulated peptide.csv cannot prove column-name parity (-10lgP, “1/k0 Range”, Area#, PTM spelling) with what PEAKS actually writes, and nothing has ever been read from a genuine Xpro export. Check in particular whether one export folder really holds all samples (the layout the fix now assumes) or whether your exports are one folder per sample
  • review the provisional class-2 quality-score thresholds (v0.20.0): frac_nested_core is scored green >= 0.50 / amber >= 0.30 at weight 3 for MHCclass = “MHC2” (quality_thresholds_default() in R/quality-score.R). Those numbers are a judgement call, not literature values - no published nested-core fraction was used. Either calibrate them on a real HLA-II dataset (the JY hla2 data in advanced plans) or tell users to run ThresholdMode = “qc_relative”, which the report already recommends. Also sanity-check the biology: is “shares a 9-mer with another ligand of the same sample” the nesting signal you would use, or would a longer/shorter k, or a per-family size, be better?
  • review the DIA calibration thresholds (v0.20.0): median_abs_rt_error green 0.5 / amber 1.5 min and median_abs_im_error green 0.010 / amber 0.030 1/k0, both weight 0.5. These are instrument- and gradient-dependent, so the defaults are only placeholders - set them from your own timsTOF runs, or leave them to qc_relative mode. Also confirm Predicted.RT is in minutes on the same scale as RT in your DIA-NN version (the metric is a plain absolute difference)
  • read the in-report Methods/Glossary prose added in v0.19.0-v0.22.0: the new nested-core and RT/IM paragraphs in 05_quality_score, the corrected PTM note in 00_mhc_report/01_id_counts, and the counting-units section of glossary.Rmd. All written by Claude; they state biology and should be read by you before the abstract is submitted
  • check the v0.22.0 abstract edits in example/abstract_eupa2026_v3.md: the motif-clarity sentence now reads “anchor-position information content for class 1, nested binding cores for class 2” and the identification-QC sentence now distinguishes DDA mass error from DIA RT/ion-mobility calibration error. Both are accurate as to what the code does, but they are longer - trim to the word limit as you see fit
  • decide on the InteractivePlots default (v0.21.0): it is FALSE, so reports look exactly as before unless asked. If interactivity is the selling point of the abstract, consider flipping the default to TRUE - but check the file sizes first (each plotly widget embeds its own JSON; the existing all-in-one reports are already 8-10 MB)
  • 2do by me, check Overlap intra-Condition seems to be showing peptides in sequences, and sequences+proteins in proteins - corrected in the individual reports, but not in the legacy main report
  • reorder plots in a way that makes more sense
  • manual checking and re-writing text by me
  • check way sample_annotation is named in the reports, should be the same as in the example
  • check which column is used as quant for each software
  • get_report_template change param order, start with template then file
  • review the 09_overview red-flag rules (v0.25.0): overview_red_flags() in R/quality-score.R flags (a) a Fail (High) / Warning (Medium) composite,
    1. any scored dimension with a sub-score < 50, i.e. past amber (High at 0),
    2. a sample with < 0.5 x the experiment median of unique peptides (depth_ratio = 0.5 is my choice, not a literature value) and (d) a Condition with a single BioReplicate (Low). On the simulated MHC-I data the only flags are Medium “Charge 1+/2+” (0.66 vs amber 0.70) - likely a quirk of the simulation, but check that rule against your real data. Are these the flags a biologist needs, and is the severity right?
  • read the 09_overview prose (v0.25.0): all captions were written by Claude and state biology - e.g. “MHC class I ligands pile up at 8-11 amino acids, usually with a sharp 9-mer peak”, “MHC class II … typically 13-17 amino acids”, Pass >= 70 = “a typical immunopeptidome”, Fail < 40 = “a failed pulldown or a non-MHC sample”. Also check the “Where to go next” table and whether 09_overview is the right name/number for the report you would hand out first
  • try compare_runs() on real runs (v0.24.0): render 05_quality_score for two or more real subsets, then compare_runs() |> plot_run_trend(). Check that the default run labels (“SampleSet | Subset”) and the default metrics (composite score, length in window, unique peptides in window) are the ones you want, and whether a dedicated cross-run report template is worth adding
  • confirm the license wording (v0.23.0): DESCRIPTION is now GPL (>= 2) and LICENSE.md the GPL-2 text; the README License section explains why (Peptides, gplots, ggcorrplot are GPL-2 only; ggupset is GPL-3). If the abstract or poster says “MIT” or just “open-source”, align it. Remember to check a new dependency’s licence before adding it

Descriptors are summarised per SAMPLE and then tested across samples (Kruskal-Wallis + pairwise Wilcoxon, BH, MedianDiff + Cliff’s delta), with a pooled peptide-level track reported alongside as explicitly descriptive; new plots plot_aa_composition / plot_aa_position_heatmap / plot_property_distribution / plot_property_sample_summary / plot_property_effectsize; new dependency Peptides (CRAN, Rcpp only) in Imports, justified as the canonical GRAVY implementation. Position-within-the-protein moved to standby (v0.16.0)

  • the provider in the templates context is now the optional Provider param: all 9 templates declare it and render the attribution through the new exported provider_line() (R/report-helpers.R), which falls back to a generic sentence naming no organisation when empty; removed the hardcoded “Immunopeptidomics Platform (IPP)” text, the personal @dkfz.de contact block and the “Code author: DGZ” lines, and gave 00_mhc_upsets the description + Code version lines it lacked. Guarded by a test that every template declares the common params and that none hardcodes an organisation/author/contact, plus a render test checking the header in both directions (v0.17.0)

  • runnable R code as a guide through: new inst/scripts/howmahico_pipeline.R + exported get_pipeline_script() (sibling of get_report_template()/get_dictionary_template()), a commented walkthrough from raw search output to rendered reports that renders via run_howmahico_report() rather than opening a template; starts in demo mode (RUN_DEMO = TRUE) running end-to-end against the shipped sim_fragpipe_dda dataset with no user data — verified: 7 focused reports in ~1 min. Plus the package’s first vignette (vignettes/howmahico.Rmd, VignetteBuilder: knitr), which gives the pkgdown site an Articles tab (v0.17.0)

  • more detailed instructions in the readme: FIXED the headline run_howmahico_report() example, which passed a Title param no template declares — rmarkdown errors on undeclared params, so it failed on copy-paste; added a Quickstart, a table of what each of the 9 reports produces, a full parameter reference (common + focused-only + the 05/06/07 sets), an output section (always-written vs CsvSave/PlotsSave tiers) and a troubleshooting table; corrected stale claims (07_pepchem missing everywhere, “mid-conversion on dev”, “~40 functions” vs 118 exports, the numbered project folders shown as repo contents, RStudio listed as a requirement instead of pandoc) (v0.17.0)

  • export a prot_all report with information condensed at the protein level: new R/prot-all.R engine (build_prot_all -> one row per protein x Sample with ligand counts, unique-peptide counts from the previously unused Is_Unique/Proteotypic flags, and Area summed on the LINEAR scale; summarise_prot_all, top_source_proteins, expand_mapped_proteins, prot_engine_columns, diann_protein_columns) + the 08_prot_all report (source proteins per sample, ligands-per-protein distribution, top source proteins, detection breadth, protein-level intensity) with 5 new plots. Protein key is a param (ProteinFeature: ProteinFirst default / GeneFirst / Accession) and MultiMapping (leading default / all) chooses how a ligand mapping to several proteins is counted. Engine-reported protein data is carried through when available (DIA-NN PG./Genes. quantities + q-values, already in pep_all but unused), by a unique-within-group rule that returns NA rather than averaging; plot_ligand_vs_protein_quant compares it against summed ligand Area. parse_diann’s protein-column select moved to any_of(diann_protein_columns()) so either DIA-NN naming generation (PG.Quantity vs PG.Abundance) survives instead of being dropped or aborting the parse. Descriptive only; no length normalisation (needs the FASTA, in standby). Also fixed: docs/ was missing from .Rbuildignore (R CMD check note after building the pkgdown site locally) (v0.18.0)

  • for PTM plots, translate unimod code into modification name: new R/ptm.R with ptm_reference() (curated UniMod accession / name / monoisotopic delta-mass table, ordered by commonness so the first match within tolerance wins on mass-degenerate pairs like Glu->pyro-Glu / Dehydrated) + translate_ptm() (vectorised over the unique tokens; payload read from inside ()/[], dispatched on UniMod-accession vs signed decimal, unmatched tokens returned UNCHANGED rather than NA), wired into plot_ptm_heatmap() as translate = TRUE (+ reference pass-through) applied where the tokens are already split so both the count and proportion branches inherit it. Both dialects are handled because a UniMod-only translation would be a silent no-op on the default FragPipe data. Display-time only — pep_all$PTM stays raw. Also fixed the wrong note in 00_mhc_report/01_id_counts (“Fragpipe and DIA-NN … UniMode PTM codes”; it is FragPipe and PEAKS that write delta masses). New test-ptm.R covers all three dialects, the Acetyl/Trimethyl tolerance boundary, PEAKS’ 2-decimal rounding, pass-through of unknown/NA/“” and the reference-order rule (v0.19.0)

  • readme: add a glossary of the column headers in pep_all + finish the in-report glossary: new pep_all_glossary() (R/report-helpers.R, 30 rows, including the misreadable parts — DIA-NN dummy ppm, computed-not-observed Mass, Accession-as-protein-group, engine-specific Score) feeding both the new shared child inst/rmarkdown/shared/glossary.Rmd (included by all ten templates before their Session & provenance footer; counting units explained with the length window interpolated from shortpep_range) and the README’s new Glossary section. Replaces 00_mhc_report’s hardcoded prose, which claimed a 12-20 AA MHC-II window (the real one is 12-25) and named 3_results/4_figures regardless of the run’s params. Guarded by two tests: every validate_pep_all() required column is documented, and so is every column the reports consume from a real build_pep_all() run on the sim data (v0.19.0)

  • class-2 motif metric + DIA identification QC: new frac_nested_core metric (internal .nested_core_fraction(): fraction of in-window ligands sharing a 9-mer - the MHC-II binding-core length - with another ligand of the same sample; one (k-mer, sequence) pair at most so internal repeats cannot make a sequence nested with itself; NA below two assessable sequences). quality_thresholds_default(“MHC2”) promotes it to the anchor metric’s weight (3, label “Nested-core families”) because anchor_information/frac_9mer are both NA for class II; weight-0 diagnostic for MHC1/MHC1_mouse. Metric keys identical across classes. Plus median_abs_rt_error / median_abs_im_error (internal .median_abs_delta()): DIA-NN’s Precursor.Mz is the LIBRARY value and report.tsv has no observed precursor m/z, so the dummy ppm cannot be repaired - its Predicted.RT/Predicted.IM (already in pep_all, unused) give the DIA analogue instead, NA for FragPipe/PEAKS and NA when every difference is 0. Both substitutions documented in 05_quality_score’s Methods; tests cover the maths, the per-class promotion, the guards, and that every scored threshold row exists in the metrics table (v0.20.0)

  • InteractivePlots (TRUE/FALSE) toggle to render compatible plots via ggplotly: new param on all ten templates; ggprint_rawr() gained an interactive arg returning plotly::ggplotly() (caller-frame name resolution and the not-generated guard kept), the shared setup + the two 00_* templates derive interactive_plots <- isTRUE(params$InteractivePlots), and the 34 call sites that print from ORDINARY chunks pass it. Plots inside results=‘asis’ tabset loops stay static on purpose (a widget printed from such a loop silently renders EMPTY without a tagList/knit_print dance - the same reason those loops use kable not DT), guarded by a test that walks every skeleton’s chunks. Unconvertible classes (ggpubr composites, seqlogos, objects already widgets) are returned unchanged, so asking for interactivity cannot break a report. 05_quality_score’s three bare prints and the four ggplotly() calls on the correlation matrices now route through the same helper, the latter with interactive = TRUE hardcoded to keep their behaviour. Verified by rendering 05_quality_score with the toggle on AND off and asserting the widget containers + embedded plotly library are present in one and absent in the other (v0.21.0)

  • check/add functionality for peaks Xpro: FOUND BROKEN and fixed - read_peaks_batch() filtered the export FOLDERS by annotation$Sample_peaks, which is the PER-SAMPLE key (a PEAKS export folder holds several samples as Area# columns, and those suffixes are what annotate_peaks() joins on), so an annotation that could be joined matched no folder at all (empty read -> “object ‘Accession’ not found” in parse_peaks()) while one naming the folder gave a silent 0-row join; folder selection now uses Sample_folder (falling back to Sample_peaks for one-folder-per-sample layouts) and both halves of the trap error out naming the two keys. Second bug: read_peaks(filedir = getwd(), folder_peaks_db = ) pasted an ABSOLUTE FolderData behind the working directory (the reports document absolute paths, and system.file() returns them) - now split with dirname()/basename(). Both were invisible because PEAKS had no end-to-end fixture, so v0.22.0 ships inst/extdata/sim_peaks_xpro/ (462 simulated peptides x 6 samples in real PEAKS shape: one export folder, -10lgP, 1/k0 Range, Area#, PEAKS-style oxidation) + tests. get_annot_peaks() documents that one row per folder is not one row per sample. Remaining for DGZ: run it on a real PEAKS 11/Xpro export (v0.22.0)

  • corrected the v0.19.0 PTM documentation: PEAKS writes the modification NAME in its PTM column (“Oxidation (M)”) and keeps the delta mass in the peptide string - it is FragPipe (delta mass) and DIA-NN (UniMod) that need translating. translate_ptm() already passed names through unchanged; the docs, the two report notes and the test comments were wrong, and a test now pins the pass-through so a PEAKS name cannot be mangled into a mass match (v0.22.0)

  • abstract wording (example/abstract_eupa2026_v3.md): motif clarity now attributed to anchor information content for class 1 and nested binding cores for class 2, and the identification-QC sentence distinguishes DDA mass error from DIA retention-time/ion-mobility calibration error (v0.22.0)

  • resolve the license conflict: relicensed MIT -> GPL (>= 2). Auditing every dependency found more than Peptides/limma: Peptides, gplots and ggcorrplot are GPL-2 ONLY, ggupset is GPL-3, limma/ggpubr GPL (>= 2). Plain GPL-3 (the option on the table) would itself have clashed with the GPL-2-only three, so the package now uses R’s own terms, GPL-2 or later, compatible with each. LICENSE.md = GPL-2 text (usethis::use_gpl_license(2, include_future = TRUE)), MIT LICENSE stub removed, README License section explains the choice; also closes the standby “license discrepancies” item (v0.23.0)

  • cross-experiment comparison: new R/compare-runs.R with compare_runs() (stacks the _scores.csv tables of N 05_quality_score renders - csv paths, results folders or score data frames; labels runs from the companion *_05_quality_score_input_params.csv as “SampleSet | Subset” and attaches MHCclass/ThresholdMode/render_timestamp/package_version; input or timestamp order; column union; WARNS on mixed MHCclass/ThresholdMode since composites are then not comparable) + summarise_runs() (per run x metric n/median/IQR + Pass/Warning/Fail counts) + plot_run_trend() (panel per metric, runs on x, box or median-trend line, QC samples as triangles, optional color_by). The 05 score csv gained a Condition column. No report template for it yet - the function + plot make the abstract’s sentence true (v0.24.0)

  • general-overview report for the biologically focused user: new 09_overview template, one page for the biologist - at-a-glance table (samples, Conditions, unique peptides all/in-window, source proteins, median score, Pass/Warning/Fail, red-flag counts), ligands per sample in/out of the length window, length histogram, composite quality score, a plain-language Red flags section and a “where to go next” table pointing at 01-08. New exported overview_red_flags() (Fail/Warning composite; any SCORED dimension past amber, worded by its label, High at sub-score 0; sample < 0.5 x median unique peptides; Condition with a single BioReplicate) and qc_samples_from_annotation() (the QCColumn lookup 05 inlined, now shared by 05 and 09). Writes _red_flags.csv. Render test in test-sim-fragpipe.R + unit tests in test-overview.R (v0.25.0)
